intro_en: HealthBench is an open-ended medical-dialogue benchmark built with 262 physicians. Its 5,000 multi-turn conversations carry 48,562 unique rubric criteria across seven themes and five behavioral axes. Conversations come from a tailored generation pipeline, physician red teaming, and HealthSearchQA rewrites, followed by relevance filtering; a model-based grader evaluates physician-authored rubrics and aggregates normalized scores.

drawio_review_note: Aligned with arXiv:2505.08775, Sections 2-4 and Appendix B, plus the official openai/simple-evals implementation. HealthBench was developed over 11 months with 262 vetted physicians across 60 countries and 26 specialties. Physician advisors chose domains and situations, wrote prompt seeds and consensus criteria, prepared training materials, and reviewed work. Most examples were generated by a tailored language-model pipeline from physician-enumerated situations; additional examples came from physician red teaming and HealthSearchQA query rewrites. Conversations alternate user and assistant turns, start and end with the user, and are filtered for realism, self-consistency, physical-health relevance, and message completeness. Physicians write positive and negative example-specific rubrics and assign theme and behavioral-axis categories; majority-supported reusable requirements form 34 consensus criteria. The final 5,000 conversations contain 48,562 unique criteria across seven themes and five axes. A model grader marks each criterion true or false; met criteria receive their signed points, the example score divides earned points by maximum positive points, and aggregate means are clipped to [0,1] with bootstrap uncertainty and slice reporting.
